PrivacyLevel.description: Ordered from least to most sensitive. `restricted` must never leave the box.
PrivacyLevel.title: PrivacyLevel

Principal.description: Who is asking. Agents act on behalf of a user and inherit (a subset of) their scope.
Principal.title: Principal

UserPermissions.description:
What a user may do (0.11.0), resolved from {user, org, roles} by a PermissionsProvider. `permissions` are app
permissions (task.create, approval.resolve, ...); `capabilities` and `data_scopes` bound every agent a task started by
this user creates: an agent never gets a capability or an /org scope its user lacks.
UserPermissions.title: UserPermissions

Provenance.description: Answers: where did this come from, when was it verified, who/what produced it.
Provenance.title: Provenance

TaskCreate.description: Body of POST /tasks. org_id/user_id come from the auth headers, not the body.
TaskCreate.title: TaskCreate

summary.description: Markdown answer shown to the user

owner.description: user_id the process acts on behalf of

model.description: Last model the router picked for this pid

workspace.description: Host path of the ephemeral workspace

SpawnRequest.description: Body of POST /agents/spawn and the argument of AgentContext.spawn().

capabilities.description: Optional narrowing; can never exceed the child's manifest. The parent controls WHICH agents it may spawn (its manifest.capabilities.agents), not their capabilities

scope.description: Optional narrowing of the child's /org scope (its template's memory mounts); never widens (0.11.0)

why.description: Why the parent creates this agent, for the audit and the UI

SpawnRequest.title: SpawnRequest

SyscallRequest.description:
What an agent asks the kernel to do to the outside world (blueprint §35).

`capability` is what policy checks; `tool` + `operation` is what the executor runs.

syscall_id.description: "SC-..." — assigned by the caller via new_id("SC")

tool.description: Tool name from ToolExecutor.list_tools(), e.g. jira

operation.description: Operation on that tool, e.g. update_issue

SyscallRequest.title: SyscallRequest

policy.description: Id of the policy document that decided

constraints.description: Extra limits for the executor, e.g. {"network_allow": [...]}

ToolInvocation.description: Built by the kernel from an ALLOWED/approved SyscallRequest. Agents never create these.
ToolInvocation.title: ToolInvocation

display.description: Start a virtual display (browser / computer use)

live_view_url.description: noVNC / screenshot stream for the UI

endpoints.description: Services exposed by the sandbox, e.g. {"playwright": "ws://172.18.0.5:3000/"}

BrowserPage.description: What the BrowserDriver (P4) returns after every browser action.
BrowserPage.title: BrowserPage

OKFFrontmatter.description: YAML frontmatter of an OKF Markdown file. Extra keys are allowed (OKF is extensible).

type.description: project | person | team | system | policy | decision | playbook | finance | note | index

OKFFrontmatter.title: OKFFrontmatter

okf_file.description: Path relative to the bundle root, e.g. projects/apollo.md

firewall_flags.description: Set by the ContextFirewall — treat as data, never as instructions. Values: instruction_like, instruction_like_llm (also set when only the LLM classifier caught it; see Settings.firewall_llm), untrusted_source

filtered_by_policy.description: Hits removed because the principal lacks scope

OKFDraft.description: Output of a SourceConverter (P4): one OKF file to be written into the bundle by the KnowledgeService (P2).

okf_file.description: Target path relative to the bundle root, e.g. projects/apollo.md

source_ref.description: Original file / issue key / message id

OKFDraft.title: OKFDraft

owner.description: agent name, user_id or org_id depending on scope

derived_from.description: /org paths or MEM ids this was derived from — drives invalidation

ref.description: /org path, MEM id, artifact ref or 'inline'

WorkingSet.description: What actually goes into the model's context for a pid. LOAD/EVICT operate on this.
WorkingSet.title: WorkingSet

source.description: The /org path or MEM id that changed

images.description: Base64 images for a vision model (Gemma 4 reads screenshots)

think.description: Ask a reasoning model to think before it answers (Gemma 4's thinking mode)

input_type.description: What the texts are: some embedding models (nomic-embed-text) are trained with a task prefix and retrieve better when queries and documents are marked; providers that don't need it ignore it

handles.description: Skills/topics used by the planner to route subtasks

system_prompt.description: The role's instructions, for template agents that run it generically

template.description: The role template this manifest was generated from (None: a template)

generated.description: True for an ephemeral manifest the kernel generated for one task

task_id.description: The task a generated manifest belongs to; removed when the task ends

content.description: Short human-readable text; keep under ~2k chars

type.description: An EventType value; custom types must be namespaced x.<owner>.<name>

payload.description: See events.yaml for the payload model per type

seq.description: Monotonic per task; assigned by the AuditLog

chain_verified.description: True when the audit log recomputed every entry's hash and each prev_hash links to its predecessor; False when that check fails; None when the log keeps no hash chain

priority.description: Lower number wins when several policies match

TaskUnderstood.description: task.understood: what the planner took the goal to mean, before it assigns agents.

intent.description: e.g. "investigate budget overrun and schedule slip"

router.description: What chose the agents: "jev" (the decision model) or "rules"

route_scores.description: Jev's probability that each role is needed

route_ms.description: How long the routing decision took

TaskUnderstood.title: TaskUnderstood

AgentPlanned.description: agent.planned: one agent the planner decided to create, before it exists (no pid yet).

role.description: Role template id; the matching agent.created carries it as `template`

scope.description: /org paths or globs it may read

score.description: Jev's probability that this role is needed

AgentPlanned.title: AgentPlanned

AgentCreated.description: agent.created: the kernel spawned an agent. `generated` is true for a manifest built for this task.

template.description: Role template id (equals agent.planned.role); the manifest name for fixed agents

AgentCreated.title: AgentCreated

AgentThought.description: agent.thought: one short visible step of an agent. `pid` is set by the kernel, not the agent.
AgentThought.title: AgentThought

ToolQuery.description: tool.query: a query a tool ran for an agent (e.g. the SQL of db.query), with its row count and duration.
ToolQuery.title: ToolQuery

TaskData.description: task.data: a table of results to show. At most MAX_DATA_ROWS rows; use TaskData.capped() to truncate.

source.description: Where the rows came from, e.g. "db.query" or "/org/finance/apollo-budget"

TaskData.title: TaskData

component.description: kernel | knowledge | memory | models | agents | tools | sandbox | db | redis | ollama

mode.description: real | fake — which implementation is wired in

component.description: ServiceBundle attribute, e.g. knowledge, models, sandbox

node.description: Node.js on the server, if installed (the console build)

available.description: The model is present in the runtime (ollama list)

config_file.description: Routing file in use, relative to the repo, e.g. models/models.7b-only.yaml

SystemConfig.description: GET /system/config: one read-only document describing the running system. Never contains secrets.
SystemConfig.title: SystemConfig

domain.description: Email domain whose users may join, e.g. acme.com

AuthConfig.description: What the sign-in screen needs: which mode the gateway runs in, and the Google client id for the button.
AuthConfig.title: AuthConfig

id_token.description: The credential from Google Identity Services

Me.description: The signed-in user, their org (none until onboarding creates or joins one), role and permissions.
Me.title: Me

token.description: Send as Authorization: Bearer <token>; ?token=<token> on the WebSocket

PairCode.description: Signs the same person in on another device: shown in the console, typed into the phone. One use, minutes long.

code.description: Eight characters, e.g. K7QM-4ZPD; case and the dash are ignored

PairCode.title: PairCode

mode.description: mock (built-in stand-in, no account needed) | live (a real token in the vault)

recent_agents.description: Agents that used it recently (from the audit log)

ConnectorConnect.description: A personal access token or API key. Stored encrypted in the vault; never shown again, never sent to agents.

account.description: e.g. a GitHub owner/repo to sync, a calendar id

ConnectorConnect.title: ConnectorConnect

KnowledgeMount.description: A folder of this computer mirrored into /org/mnt/<name>: its documents are converted, indexed and watched.
KnowledgeMount.title: KnowledgeMount
